answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly audited claim is proven false. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and immobilize tokens for every extra identity, making a large fake swarm costly rather than free; spreading identities across umber and ivory teams does not evade the shared stake rule. Audits can ripple from one failed claim to related submissions, raising the expected loss without assuming identities are easy to distinguish.
